segments.summary: Prompt, attachment, storage, verification-gate, and visible recovery contracts are explicit; structured enforcement remains authoritative over advisory extraction.
Logging and request metadata are bounded, while pattern accuracy, false-positive recovery, performance, provider parsing, and exploratory overrides lack closed acceptance or authority contracts.
Allowlist, fallback, exact approval, chained-command, and Git protections are strong; SQL detection and guard-rate limiting leave consequential behavior and state open.
GUI authority, exact approval UX, prompt ownership, runner ordering, realpath failure, and operation tagging form a coherent cross-layer contract.
Request-local scope and canonical GUI placement are explicit, but path extraction, interview relaxation defaults, and cleanup precedence expose security and recovery ambiguity.
Advanced-card authority and runtime propagation are well bounded; approval-card lifecycle and partial GUI persistence/apply states require further closure.
Canonical history, safe persistence, path scope, cleanup propagation, and operation metadata are clear; gate detail schemas and sensitive cleanup edge cases remain incomplete.
Metadata, GUI wiring, and worktree path gaps are explicitly closed; interview tag authority, event correlation, documentation parsing, and async performance remain open.
